attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No method is known to prove that the real SAT-labelled quotient functional avoids all subthreshold low-degree feature sketches. Random-incidence or random-label counting does not transfer to SAT.
steps: Start with the quotient incidence representation H_N(z)=<A_N(z),y_N> over F_2, where y_N is the SAT label vector on generated quotient classes.
Cycle 56 handled the case A_N(z) lies in a low-rank affine subspace or in a small computable codebook; then hardwired basis parities or table entries compute H_N.
Generalize: suppose a small circuit T_N computes r_N features and the composed label functional <A_N(z),y_N> equals a degree-t polynomial P_N(T_N(z)) except on E_N inputs.
Implement T_N once, hardwire all coefficients of P_N, compute all degree-at-most-t monomials, XOR selected monomials, and patch the E_N exceptional inputs by equality tests.

This yields C(H_N)<=S_T+O(sum_{i<=t} binom(r_N,i))+O(E_NN). Hence for r_N=N^alpha, S_T=N^s, E_N=N^eta, constant t, the source lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} is falsified whenever max{s,alpha t,1+eta}<1+epsilon.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is an upper-bound conservation law and an audit gate. It sharpens the route-specific obstruction but does not establish the required barely-superlinear lower bound for H_N and therefore does not prove P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: XOR quotient carrier, low-degree feature-sketch gate

assumptions: Circuits are nonuniform Boolean circuits of fan-in two unless a restricted class is explicitly named.
The quotient universe identifies length-L formulas only by SAT-preserving equivalence relevant to the parity incidence vector; duplicate even multiplicities cancel over F_2.
A feature sketch consists of a circuit T_N:{0,1}^N -> {0,1}^{r_N} of size S_T and an arbitrary hardwired F_2 polynomial P_N of degree at most t in r_N variables.
The representation may fail on E_N inputs; equality patches of size O(E_N N) are charged explicitly.
definitions: source object: H_N^{xor}(z)=\oplus_{j\le M_N} SAT(F_{N,j}(z)) on N input bits, with M_N=\lfloor N^q\rfloor and query length L=(\log N)^d, d>1.
target object: SAT lower bounds against P/poly, hence NP not subset P/poly, obtained only through the XOR carrier substitution bridge.
controlled interface: a P/poly generator G_N of size N^rho outputs the M_N length-L SAT queries; a SAT circuit of size L^c is substituted independently into every generated query.
target-preserving condition: max{rho,q}<1+epsilon and L=(\log N)^d ensure every fixed SAT exponent c contributes only N^{o(1)} overhead, with no nonuniform advice depending on z beyond G_N.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: There is no size-preserving compiler from unrestricted m^k-size Boolean circuits for F_{t,b} to protocols whose cost is below the linear communication ceiling.
steps: Define F_{t,b}=SAT_t(IP_b(x_1,y_1),...,IP_b(x_t,y_t)) with b>=C log t and total length m=2tb.
Use the projected OR slice inside SAT_t to obtain R_dt(SAT_t)=Omega(t).
Apply the lifting theorem to get R_cc(F_{t,b})=Omega(tb)=Omega(m).
Observe that SAT_t uniformly projects to F_{t,b}, so the lifted carrier is NP-hard and remains in NP.
Try to infer F_{t,b} notin SIZE(m^k) from the communication lower bound.
The inference stalls because ordinary two-party communication is always at most m+1, and any lower bound obtained from it is at most linear in the lifted length.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The route proves a valid communication lower bound for an NP-hard lifted language, but P vs NP requires excluding polynomial-size circuits; the certified threshold is O(m), not m^k for k>1.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: Lifted Communication Threshold Collapse

assumptions: Choose b>=C log t for a gadget family where the relevant lifting theorem is known.
Use a SAT_t encoding that contains a linear-size OR_t projection, giving R_dt(SAT_t)=Omega(t) for the queried slice.
The reduction SAT_t <=_m^p F_{t,b} fixes gadget inputs uniformly and increases length from t to m=Theta(tb).
The only attempted transfer to SIZE(m^k) is through ordinary two-party communication complexity under the same input partition.

target object: the two-party lifted language F_{t,b}=h(g_b(x_1,y_1),...,g_b(x_t,y_t)) under the block partition, and unrestricted Boolean circuits SIZE(m^k) only through an explicit circuit-to-protocol transfer.
controlled interface: a deterministic or randomized lifting theorem for a gadget g_b such as IP_b or IND_b, plus a separately named compiler turning target circuits into low-communication protocols.

target-preserving condition: SAT_t must project to F_{t,b} by fixing one side of every gadget, with length m=Theta(tb), polynomial-time uniformity, and no nonuniform advice encoded in the fixed gadget side.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No construction is known for an advice-free, low-D, cap-compatible generator of rows and nonblackbox anti-ball proofs. Proof-system soundness and the row generator may hide exactly the lower bound being extracted.
steps: Encode AntiBall(T,s,r) by a formula Phi_{m,T,s,r} asserting that there exists a circuit C of size s and an edit set E of size at most r such that C agrees with T outside E.
Observe that unsatisfiability of Phi_{m,T,2^{epsilon m},2^{rho m}} is exactly the anti-ball condition needed for exact MCSP hardness above 2^{epsilon m}.

Replace the prior black-box certificate by a generated proof pi of unsatisfiability in a sound proof system P; verification may be exponential in m but remains compatible with E if the row/proof pair is generated rather than searched.

Use the low-image rank i and data input x to define L(i,x)=T_{m,i}(x). If L has circuits of size 2^{delta(1+D)m}, fixing i gives a circuit for the hard row, contradicting anti-ball soundness when delta<epsilon/(1+D).
Apply kappa-padding to obtain all target lengths with exponent delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
Attempt to drop the generator and rely only on existence of a P-proof; exhaustive search over proof strings of length 2^{mu m} costs 2^{2^{mu m}}, which exceeds E and breaks target preservation.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a valid route-level bridge and quarantine result, not a proof of P != NP. The decisive source theorem remains missing: produce a sparse non-large generated anti-ball proof family without subthreshold row decoding or nonuniform advice.

assumptions: epsilon,D,kappa are fixed positive constants with epsilon<1 and D=O(1).
The verifier's soundness is mathematical, not just heuristic or average-case over circuits.
Canonical unranking of distinct rows is E-uniform and does not use nonuniform advice.
Source lengths are kappa-dense: every sufficiently large target length is padded from some m within factor kappa.
If proofs have length 2^{mu m}, they are generated or streamed; they are not found by exhaustive proof search.
definitions: source object: an E-uniform low-image family (T_{m,i},pi_{m,i}) with i<2^{D m}, generated or sequentially emitted in 2^{O(m)} time, not merely existentially certified.
target object: a multiplexed E language L(i,x)=T_{m,i}(x) with final input length n=(1+D)m up to kappa-padding.
controlled interface: a sound nonblackbox anti-ball verifier V whose acceptance implies distance from all unrestricted circuits at the declared size threshold.
target-preserving condition: row/proof generation is advice-free, kappa-dense, low-image, and has no subthreshold bit decoder that would itself give circuits below 2^{epsilon m}.
anti-ball soundness means every accepted row, or at least one canonically hard accepted row used by the multiplexer, is outside the Hamming ball around every small circuit.
barrier posture: the generated low-image source is non-large, so it is outside the direct natural-proofs template unless the verifier acceptance expands to a dense constructive property.

The radius rho is not charged for exact MCSP hardness when the forbidden centers already have size 2^{epsilon m}.

control_decision.reason: The bridge is now target-preserving and quantitatively stable, while two invalid repairs are quarantined: existential exponential proofs and low-query black-box transcripts.

dependency_updates.description: The carrier may now use generated nonblackbox anti-ball proofs; proof length is separated from extraction exponent when generation is E-uniform.
The extracted exponent remains delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)); rho is not charged for exact MCSP when forbidden centers already have size 2^{epsilon m}.
Explicitness is now row/proof generation, not existential proof availability. Long generated proofs are allowed; long searched proofs are quarantined.
Low-query transcript certificates require q=Omega(2^{epsilon m}/m), so short black-box anti-ball proofs are invalid.
The low-D generated family is non-large, but any dense constructive extension of the verifier acceptance would become a natural-property obstruction.
dependency_updates.status: outside known barrier only if sparsity is preserved

falsifiers: falsifier: anti-ball proofs exist only existentially at length 2^{mu m}; canonical proof search is super-E and the target language is not validly defined.
falsifier: the verifier is black-box in T and reads q=o(2^{epsilon m}/m) locations, since a zero-fill completion has circuit O(qm).
falsifier: the row generator gives random access circuits of size 2^{alpha m} with alpha<epsilon, contradicting the claimed MCSP no-side threshold.
falsifier: the proof or table constants are supplied as nonuniform advice depending on m or on the selected row.
falsifier: the verifier acceptance expands into a dense P/poly-constructive property rejecting small circuits, triggering the natural-proofs obstruction under pseudorandom functions.
falsifier: the anti-ball formula forbids only centers below 2^{epsilon m-rho m} while the extraction claims threshold 2^{epsilon m}; this is an invalid radius accounting step.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: Generated proofs remain compatible with E extraction for any constant mu because L computes row bits from the generator, while existential proofs become unusable as soon as mu>0. If the verifier degenerates to q low-load table queries, the zero-fill falsifier appears regardless of mu.
held_fixed_controls: epsilon=0.40 as the forbidden circuit-size exponent over m input bits.
rho=0.05 with centers still at size 2^{epsilon m}, so exact MCSP extraction pays no radius loss.
D=0.03 distinct-image entropy for the row family.
kappa=1 for the first audit before padding losses.
unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits are the lower-bound target model.
the row generator is advice-free and has no random-access circuit exponent below epsilon.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The route has moved from black-box certificates to nonblackbox binding; a concrete proof-complexity carrier test is needed to separate valid generated proofs from invalid existential proof folklore.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: For each m, build the approximate-MCSP unsatisfiability formula Phi_{m,T,2^{epsilon m},2^{rho m}} for a kappa-dense, low-image table family T_{m,i}. Imagine a sound proof system P and a sequential generator that emits (T_{m,i},pi_{m,i}) where pi_{m,i} is a P-proof of unsatisfiability.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A formal certificate must include E-uniform row/proof generation, soundness of P for Phi, correctness of the Phi-to-anti-ball encoding, low-D canonical unranking, and a leakage audit proving no subthreshold row decoder or advice channel is present.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: proof-length exponent mu in |pi_{m,i}|=2^{mu m}, comparing generated proofs against merely existential proofs.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 57 separates proof length from proof location. A nonblackbox anti-ball proof can be long without harming the MCSP-to-E extraction if the row/proof pair is E-uniformly generated; an existential long proof is not valid because locating it is double-exponential. The route's next hard obligation is a generated, sparse, non-large anti-ball proof family, not another hardness-magnification slogan.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Instantiate Phi_{m,T,s,r} for one restricted proof system, such as resolution or algebraic IPS with explicit row constants, and test whether any generated low-D family can have short nonblackbox unsat proofs without giving a local decoder for T.

The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
